A-01.location: s-06, check k-08 (index.html l.327 prompt, l.331 reveal)
A-01.evidence: The prompt reads "Why isn't English's grouping (sleeper with seer) more logical than Basque's (sleeper with seen)?" The reveal reads "Basque groups by 'who the event happens to': the sleeper and the seen are both simply undergoing… and only an agent acting on someone else gets marked." In Basque, 'sleep' is normally *lo egin* ('do sleep'), which is formally transitive: ergative subject plus *du*. Martínez-Areta (2019, ASJU, ojs.ehu.eus/index.php/ASJU/article/download/22416/20379) cites 'do sleep' and 'do snoring' as verbs whose transitive morphology comes from their origin. Wiktionary/kaikki lists the auxiliary *du* for *lo egin*. Unergative intransitives also take -k with du. Baker (mmll.cam.ac.uk/files/copil_11_1_baker.pdf) gives "Gizonak dantza egin du" ('the man danced'), and the Lund Basque grammar paper gives "Neskak dantzatu du" ('the girl has danced'). Berro (2012) says a group of unergatives takes ergative subjects across dialects. A reader leaves with the false belief that a Basque sleeper is bare. They also learn that Basque marks only agents who act on someone else. The facts file has no claim about sleep in Basque (c-05 and c-12 cover only arrive/come/fall/appear).
A-01.expected_fix: Option 1 is to make the k-08 prompt and reveal general: "…than an ergative language's (sleeper with seen)". Then keep Basque's real examples, such as "Basque groups the one who arrives with the one who is seen". Option 2 is to swap 'sleeper' for 'arriver/comer' wherever the text attributes the grouping to Basque. Also soften "only an agent acting on someone else gets marked" to "mainly the agent of a two-participant verb gets marked". A one-line caveat would be optional and fits the active/stative "mention" scope: "even Basque gives -k to some agent-like one-participant verbs, like 'dance'".
A-01.closure_evidence: Source and probe (390px; scroll to and click `[data-check=k-08] [data-reveal]`, then read `.d-feedback`; screenshot run/screenshots/probe/r2acc-k08-reveal.png) give: prompt "Why isn't English's grouping (sleeper with seer) more logical than an ergative language's (sleeper with seen)?"; reveal "An ergative language groups by 'who the event happens to'… the marking goes mainly to the agent of a two-participant verb. In Basque, that's why the one who arrives and the one who is seen both stay bare, while the one who sees gets -k." That matches c-05/c-12 (arrive/come are absolutive) and is consistent with ergative unergatives such as *lo egin* and *dantza egin*. The echo for the S+P pick now says "That's the ergative grouping, S with P… (In Basque's own examples: the one who arrives goes with the one who is seen.)" The k08 echo says "matches the ergative grouping". The meta description says "group the lone participant with the one who is seen", and the k-01 feedback says the same. Running `grep -i "sleep|slept|sleeper"` over the site finds no sentence that attributes sleep marking to Basque. The recap's Basque card uses "Martin etorri da" ('Martin has come'). The disposition's claims check out.

A-02.location: s-02, aside "Why not just say 'subject' and 'object'?" (index.html l.110)
A-02.evidence: "English shows the grouping only on pronouns." English verb agreement also groups S with A ("The man sleeps", "The man sees the dogs": -s agrees with S/A, never with P). c-02's note limits "only pronouns" to case forms.
A-02.expected_fix: "English shows the grouping in its word forms only on pronouns" (or "…its case forms only on pronouns").
A-02.closure_evidence: The text now reads "Also, English shows the grouping in its word forms only on pronouns." That scopes the claim to form or case, so it no longer rules out verb agreement.

A-03.closure_evidence: The paragraph reads "Only the tense changed (strictly, the aspect), from 'sells' to 'has sold'…", which is consistent with c-10 (perfective aspect) and the "tense/aspect" in the k-07 feedback. P-01.criterion: engagement where intended (k-07 predict commits before reveal); misconception handling
P-01.evidence: Probe m5-locked.png (390px, before k-07 is answered). The locked switch renders the "sells" sentence at 45% opacity: "laṛkā pustak bēctā hai", tag "A: NO MARKER", plus the footnote "The noun's own ending also shifts (laṛkā → laṛkē) before -nē." It sits directly under the k-07 options (m4-k07-before.png). A reader glancing down can rule out A ("in both") and C ("only in sells") before committing, and A is exactly the misconception k-07's feedback targets. The click on "has sold" correctly times out while locked, so ac-09 is met.
P-01.expected_fix: Hide the whole sentence (agent tag and footnote included) while `.is-locked`. Show a neutral placeholder instead, e.g. greyed chips with no tag, or just the lock line. Reveal everything on the k-07 commit.
P-01.closure_evidence: c2m-k07-locked.png and c2m-ss-locked.png (390). Under the k-07 options, the widget shows the segmented control plus a dashed panel reading "Answer the question above to unlock the switch." There is no sentence, agent tag or footnote. The probe text of `#split-switch` while locked is just "Hindi-Urdu / sells / has sold / Answer the question above…". I picked A (the tempting wrong answer): the feedback starts "Not quite. The answer is B." and explains the A misconception. Then the switch unlocked (c2m-ss-unlocked.png). Clicking "has sold" showed "laṛkē-nē … A: ERGATIVE -NĒ" (c2m-ss-sold.png). CSS: widgets/w-split-switch/index.css l.34–36 hide `.ss-sent`, `.ss-tr` and `.ss-foot`.

P-03.criterion: ux-ui §7 / plan s-05 figure ("three side-by-side cards ... so they can be compared")
P-03.evidence: `.d-wide` only applies to direct children of `.d-main`. `.lang-cards`, `#f-recap` and `.recap` are inside `<section>`, so they stay at the prose measure (~605px). With page.css line 255 `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr))`, the cards fall 2+1 at 1100 and 1280, with Dyirbal orphaned on its own row (d1-cards.png, r1100-cards.png). The reader can't scan the three splits in one row, which is what the plan asked for.
P-03.expected_fix: Make `.d-wide` apply to `.d-main .d-wide` (or move these blocks out of the section wrapper). At ≥ 900px with the wide measure, use the intended `repeat(3, minmax(0,1fr))`. Below 900px keep the single column.
P-03.closure_evidence: At 1100 (c2w1100-cards.png) and 1280 (c2w1280-rail-s05.png) Kurdish, Georgian and Dyirbal sit in one row, so all three splits can be scanned together. At 768 (c2w768-cards.png) the cards are a clean single column. The `.d-main .d-wide` override lets the block exceed the prose measure (cards span about 324–1224px at 1280).

P-07.evidence: From the initial "?" state, the first tap always adds -k, so choosing "bare" (the right answer in puzzle 1 and for every P) takes two taps. The state label under the chip ("with -k" → "bare") does make this recoverable.
P-07.expected_fix: Change the hint to "Tap to switch between -k and bare", or have the first tap pick "bare" so it cycles bare → -k.
P-07.closure_evidence: c2m-dec0.png (390). The label under the chip reads "TAP: -K ⇄ BARE", and the hint reads "Tap the noun to switch it between -k and bare. First tap adds -k." Taking two taps to reach "bare" is now signposted. The builder's reason for keeping -k first (not biasing the default toward the puzzle-1/P answer) is pedagogically sound, and the hint-text option was one of the fixes I offered.
